---
title: "Exit codes"
weight: 5
---

<!-- Generated by `just docs` from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every command exits with one of these codes. The code comes from the kind of the error, never from its message, so a script can rely on it. The error itself goes to stderr: `Error:` and the message, then one `Try:` line with the next step.

| Code | Kind | Meaning | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 |  | Done. | A command did its job. Help printed. An attach ended with a detach, or with the agent's end. |
| 1 | `failed` | The command could not do its job. | A host did not answer. The helper failed. No hosts yet. A connection that closed. An error that is not a user error. |
| 2 | `usage` | The command line or a config file is wrong. | An unknown command or flag. A missing or extra argument. A bad value. Two flags that conflict. A name that matches two sessions. A `hosts.toml` that does not decode. |
| 3 | `not_found` | A named thing does not exist. | No host, session, agent, provider, template or secret of that name. |
| 4 | `needs_answer` | The command needs an answer, and input is off. | `setup` without a terminal, and without the flags that answer its questions. `new` without a terminal, for a folder that does not exist on the host. |
| 5 | `refused` | A policy or a tier refuses the action. | None in this release. |
| 130 | `cancelled` | The user or a signal cancelled. | The answer no. A question of `host add` or `host destroy` that reads no answer, as in a script. Ctrl+C or SIGTERM outside an attach. |

The shell reports a process that a signal ended as 128 plus the signal's number, so Ctrl+C outside an attach gives 130. The client gives 130 for SIGTERM too, because both are a cancel.
